scoreContext: Comparative visual evidence against original and fixed target, not numeric approval thresholds. Native registration/field correctness is assessed separately from the finished visible art.
observations: Useful progress: the old nearly black lower horizontal band is removed, the lower body stays blue, and there are genuine native relief courses. The narrow terrain identity, palette family and grounded shape remain recognizable.

N/S heroes at published2x and logical128 still read as a broad slab with a few soft rectangular relief blocks. The upper cyan zone occupies roughly published y298-362 across x64-320 and is nearly uniform. Lower relief near x90-295/y360-538 blends into the backing with soft muddy shoulders. The target demonstrates larger differentiated rounded/faceted stone volumes rather than shallow block embossing.

E/W heroes read as thin cyan bars with limited surface information: the large top/end regions are very flat in value and plane definition. The expected thin profile is preserved, but its interior shape and material do not yet give the same substantial softly lit stone character as the broad views should.

At phone32 in both portrait and landscape, the front courses reduce to a repetitive blue brick-like glyph. The silhouette is identifiable, but individual stone masses and useful plane/highlight separation are weaker than the frozen desired outcome. Enlarging or adding tiny decoration would not solve this.

The candidate maintains readable cyan/cobalt colors and avoids black pits, blown highlights and directional cast shadows. It lacks a useful broad highlight hierarchy over the stone planes; the near-flat cyan upper field and muted lower faces make the result feel unfinished beside the fixed target.

True native and independently composed joins are close and no local port gap, opaque cut-cap stripe or alpha puncture was found in the bounded checks. The supplied E/W detail crop also includes an interior stone groove near expanded published y550; the actual top port crossings are y473.344 and729.344 and are clean. This interior groove is not reported as a port defect.

The actual saved linked material uses a normalized native normal field and opaque normal-dependent hemispheric radiance. This was within the frozen preconstruction method freedom. Its use of an emission output, inactive area lights or differing graph identity is not a blocker; the requested revision concerns the actual visible form and finish.

blockers.location: N/S broad body and upper course; E/W top/end regions; repeated logical128 and phone32 views
blockers.effect: The model reads as a flat wall carrying shallow soft rectangular relief. It does not yet achieve the substantial rounded/faceted, interlocking blue stone masses established by the frozen definition of good.
blockers.desiredVisibleOutcome: Develop stronger purposeful stone volumes and clearer large plane changes within the same finite strip, exact ports/collars and grounded envelope. Make the courses feel like coherent stone construction rather than blocks embossed into a slab; the large masses must remain readable at cell128 and32. The editor chooses geometry, normals and other native methods; no target part count or copied crack arrangement is required.

blockers.location: Nearly uniform cyan upper region in N/S (published roughly x64-320/y298-362), and long flat cyan top/end zones in E/W; muted lower relief transitions
blockers.effect: The current color/illumination response gives too little light-to-midtone structure to explain rounded stone planes. The lower relief edges look soft and merged, and the finish is materially less developed than the selected cartoon target.
blockers.desiredVisibleOutcome: Create broad soft, controlled plane/edge highlights, readable cobalt midtones and sparse deeper blue recesses so stone forms separate cleanly without white glare, black outlining, microtexture or a preferred horizontal key. Preserve the now-readable blue base and clean all-view collars/ports. This is an outcome request and does not prescribe a Principled shader, literal graph, particular light rig or extra decoration.

remainingDifferences: Exact target stone counts, cracks, decorations and single-view silhouette are not locks. A coherent alternate native construction is acceptable.
The narrow E/W proportions follow the real finite source/profile contract and are not a demand to widen the barrier.

Slight native-versus-independent contour coverage and up-to-one-level opaque RGB residuals are retained honestly; these did not reveal a local visible seam defect and do not waive defects in a future candidate.
